recipes.name: Cucumber Sandwiches
ingredients_raw: 1 (1 pound) loaf sliced bread, crusts removed

steps.text: Place cucumber slices between 2 paper towels set in a colander. Allow liquid to drain, about 10 minutes.
Mix cream cheese, mayonnaise, garlic powder, onion salt, and Worcestershire sauce in a bowl until smooth.
Spread cream cheese mixture evenly on one side of each bread slice.
Divide cucumber slices over half of the bread slices; sprinkle lemon pepper on cucumber.
Stack the other half of the bread slices spread-side down over cucumber to make sandwiches; slice into triangles.

raw_recipe.headline: Cucumber Sandwiches
raw_recipe.description: Crustless cucumber sandwiches with cream cheese spread; cut into triangles or rounds for elegant sandwiches—perfect for parties or afternoon tea!

review.reviewBody: Great spread. I actually combined this recipe with another. I used the spread to put on a toasted pita, then added cucumers and bacon. It was awsome!
Having never tried these before, I thought they were pretty good, if not a little bland. Next time I will definitely be adding dill!!!

I altered a bit but this was a great starting recipe. I mixed worcestershire, fresh lemon juice, garlic salt, black pepper, and cream cheese for the spread. Added fresh mint on each cucumber slice for a light fresh taste.

Literally one of the best things ever! I make this for every occasion where it will be even a little bit acceptable. However, I do tend to alter the recipe just a tad, adding more of the garlic and Worcestershire sauce to taste.

I added fresh chopped dill to the cream cheese and placed a small sprig on the top of each sandwich. I also slice the cucumbers a little thicker than recommended because my guests prefer the clean crisp bite of the cucumber with the cheese. I use a biscuit cutter, the size of the cucumber to cut out the bread. I use a hand mixer to whip the cheese to make it lighter and use about 1/8 of cup of mayo. I use English cucumbers because they have less seeds. I use onion powder rather than onion salt.

Awesome! I was craving cucumbers, but I was out of bread, so I used the sweet rolls I made earlier today. I wasn't sure how that would turn out, but the flavors together were amazing. I made the recipe as written, except for one *tiny* addition, dill. I just like cucumbers with dill.
This was so refreshing, and it so hit the spot. Thank you for sharing!

Made for classic English Tea to celebrate Christmas with a large group of women. Well received. Adjusted the seasonings to include a dash of cayenne powder. Prepared cheese filling the night before. Filled full size sandwiches with cheese on both slices adding thin sliced cucumber and dashes of lemon pepper and dill to only one slice. Joined plain cheese haves with cucumber halves. Removed crust from bread and cut into quarters with electric knife before serving. Found this method created fully filled small sandwiches of an attractive appearance.
I made these for a brunch and they were a huge hit. I added an extra dash of Worcestershire and made open face sandwiches on party pumpernickel. Delicious, easy to follow recipe. It's a winner!

this came out very tasty. cant wait to try it tomorrow after its sat overnight. i followed other reviews and used a little less mayo, and then added a sprinkle of dill on top of the cucumber. Made these for a "moms day" in our preschool room and they were a hit :)
i used onion powder and garlic salt, since thats what i had on hand and it worked out great

I've been searching for something reminiscent to the English tea sandwiches we had during tea time, abroad, for quite some time. To make it "proper," I used a petite pumpernickel loaf with the crusts trimmed, sprinkled each sandwich with dill and served them open face. My daughter really enjoyed it during tea time (something I still do, daily) & we'll be serving them at my tea party baby shower this coming weekend. Thanks for sharing!

I served these sandwiches at a Bridal Tea that I hosted and they were a hit! I'm saving this recipe as we'll definitely want to make these for everyday. I sweated my cucumbers a few hours prior to assembling the sandwiches. We assembled the sandwiches right before serving and garnished with fresh violets.

These were okay, but bland. I wasn't a fan of the worcestershire flavor, and it seemed like something was missing. I did use the lemon pepper and it was fine. This was okay, but I have another recipe I prefer. I just didn't want to look for it and I always enjoy trying out someone else's version. I added some dill weed too to see if that's what was missing.
Worth the effort for a lil sandwich 💖

Had cucumber teas sandwiches at a baby shower one time and fell in love with them. decided to give this a try. i had to use up green onions before they went bad so my onion powder was replaced by the green onions. these sandwiches were delish. such a nice item to have even for a supper with some fresh fruit on a hot summer day.

I add dill and use a flavored cream cheese like vegetable or one of the other flavors. Also for a sweet one use strawberry cream cheese and fresh strawberries sliced thin! I add powdered sugar to the cream cheese.
I added fresh minced garlic and fresh dill. Was a great summertime hit.
This was good, but I'll use less spice next time. Thought it was a little overpowering.

Delightfully refreshing and crisp! Keep quite well as leftovers for a little while. The only change I might make is adding a bit of dill to the cream cheese spread mixture. Other than that near perfect!

I thought it was very refreshing and easy to make. I did substitute the Worcestershire sauce and lemon pepper for a dash of fresh lemon juice and one packet of crystalized lemon . I do not like Worcestershire sauce.

I was excited to try this recipe. It was easy to make. I thought is was just okay-worth making one time. Maybe if I made the spread the night before and let it practiced-it may be more flaorful? Thank you for the recipe! :)
